plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (MgF2/HfO2 chirped mirror stack) based on feedback directives. Four routes explore: (1) constrained linear chirp with tight per-layer variance bounds as directed, (2) periodic 1-D photonic crystal structure with AR matching layers per evidence, (3) increased layer count chirped stack for broader stopband coverage, (4) alternative HfO2/SiO2 material pair for improved UV transparency. All routes maintain 255-280 nm passband, 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm stopbands, fused silica substrate, no metals, ≤30 layers.

routes.title: Constrained linear chirp MgF2/HfO2 stack with tight variance bounds
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A constrained linear chirp trajectory (thickness decaying from ~140 nm to ~50 nm across 20 layers) with strict per-layer variance bounds (±5 nm) will suppress large-amplitude stochastic jumps and guide the optimizer toward a physically meaningful manifold, improving target score convergence compared to the unconstrained chirp in route_02.
routes.design_principle: Initialize thickness variables on a smooth linear chirp path and apply tight bounds to restrict search to a narrow manifold around this trajectory, reducing optimizer exploration of non-physical thickness combinations while preserving optimization freedom within the manifold.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | fused silica substrate (20 finite layers total, alternating MgF2/HfO2 starting with MgF2)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: tight thickness tolerance (±5 nm) requires precise deposition control
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
expected_advantages: Tighter bounds reduce search space and improve convergence
Linear chirp initialization provides physically meaningful starting point
May achieve higher target score than route_02's unconstrained approach
known_risks: Tight bounds may prevent optimizer from finding global optimum if chirp trajectory is suboptimal
20 layers may be insufficient for simultaneous 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm rejection
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer alternating MgF2/HfO2 stack on fused silica substrate under air incidence. Layer sequence: MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2, MgF2, HfO2 (20 finite layers). Initialize thicknesses on a linear chirp from 140 nm (layer 1) to 50 nm (layer 20). Apply per-layer thickness bounds of ±5 nm around the chirp trajectory. Optimize all 20 thicknesses to maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing mean transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Evaluate coherent TMM response across 255-1100 nm spectrum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Direct response to feedback directives: implement constrained linear chirp trajectory with tight per-layer variance bounds (±5 nm) to suppress large-amplitude stochastic jumps observed in route_02 and force optimizer into physically meaningful search manifold.

routes.title: Periodic 1-D photonic crystal MgF2/HfO2 stack with AR matching layers
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic stack structure with anti-reflection matching layers on both sides, based on the 1-D photonic crystal filter design principle from evidence, will achieve better passband transmission and stopband rejection than a pure chirped stack by leveraging constructive interference in the passband and photonic bandgap effects in the stopband.
routes.design_principle: Construct periodic main-function units (L/2 H L/2) repeated m times, sandwiched between input and output AR matching layers. Optimize layer thicknesses using TMM to position the photonic bandgap over 300-1100 nm while maintaining a transmission window at 255-280 nm.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | AR_input_L | AR_input_H | AR_input_L | [Main_L/2 | Main_H | Main_L/2] repeated 6 times | AR_output_L | AR_output_H | AR_output_L | fused silica substrate (24 finite layers total: 3 AR input + 18 main function + 3 AR output)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: AR layers require precise thickness tuning
expected_advantages: Periodic structure provides well-defined photonic bandgap for stopband
Evidence-supported design family for solar-blind UV filters
known_risks: Periodic structure may have narrower stopband than chirped design
24 layers may not provide sufficient rejection depth for both visible and NIR bands simultaneously
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer periodic MgF2/HfO2 stack on fused silica substrate under air incidence. Structure: 3-layer AR input (MgF2, HfO2, MgF2), followed by 6 repetitions of main-function unit (MgF2/2, HfO2, MgF2/2), followed by 3-layer AR output (MgF2, HfO2, MgF2). Total 24 finite layers. Optimize 9 independent thickness variables (AR input L, AR input H, AR input L2, Main L/2, Main H, Main L/2 duplicate, AR output L, AR output H, AR output L2) with symmetry constraints where applicable. Maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing mean transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. Use gradient-based optimizer. Evaluate coherent TMM response across 255-1100 nm. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Alternative topology to route_02's chirped approach: implements evidence-based 1-D photonic crystal design with periodic main-function units and AR matching layers to leverage photonic bandgap effects for stopband rejection.

routes.title: Increased layer count chirped MgF2/HfO2 stack for broader stopband
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing the layer count from 20 to 28 layers in a chirped MgF2/HfO2 stack will provide additional degrees of freedom to simultaneously suppress both 300-700 nm visible and 700-1100 nm NIR bands while maintaining 255-280 nm passband transmission, addressing the insufficient rejection depth observed in route_02.
routes.design_principle: Extend the chirped mirror concept with more layers to broaden the effective stopband. Thickness chirp spans a wider range to cover both visible and NIR rejection requirements. Additional layers provide more interference opportunities for out-of-band suppression.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | fused silica substrate (28 finite layers total, alternating MgF2/HfO2 starting with MgF2)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: increased layer count increases deposition time and complexity
theory_basis: Stopband width scales with layer count and index contrast
expected_advantages: More layers provide broader stopband coverage
Additional degrees of freedom enable simultaneous visible and NIR rejection
known_risks: Increased layer count may reduce passband transmission due to cumulative absorption/scatter
Optimization complexity increases with more variables
May approach 30-layer limit leaving no margin for additional AR layers
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 28-layer alternating MgF2/HfO2 stack on fused silica substrate under air incidence. Layer sequence: MgF2, HfO2 repeated 14 times (28 finite layers total). Initialize thicknesses on a linear chirp from 160 nm (layer 1) to 40 nm (layer 28) to cover broader wavelength range. Apply per-layer thickness bounds of ±15 nm around the chirp trajectory. Optimize all 28 thicknesses to maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing mean transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Evaluate coherent TMM response across 255-1100 nm spectrum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Addresses route_02's limited rejection depth by increasing layer count from 20 to 28, providing more degrees of freedom for simultaneous visible and NIR band suppression while maintaining the chirped stack topology.

routes.title: HfO2/SiO2 chirped stack for improved UV transparency
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing MgF2 with SiO2 in the low-index layer position while retaining HfO2 as high-index will improve UV transparency in the 255-280 nm passband due to SiO2's excellent UV transmission properties, while maintaining sufficient index contrast for stopband rejection.
routes.design_principle: Use HfO2/SiO2 material pair instead of MgF2/HfO2. HfO2 provides high index (~2.0-2.2 in UV), SiO2 provides low index (~1.5) with excellent UV transparency. Apply same chirped stack topology as route_02 but with improved passband material properties.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | fused silica substrate (20 finite layers total, alternating HfO2/SiO2 starting with HfO2)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: SiO2 matches substrate material for reduced interface stress
theory_basis: Material dispersion and absorption in UV range
expected_advantages: SiO2 has better UV transparency than MgF2 below 280 nm
SiO2 matches fused silica substrate for thermal/mechanical compatibility
known_risks: Lower index contrast (HfO2~2.0 vs SiO2~1.5) than MgF2/HfO2 may reduce stopband rejection
HfO2 may have higher absorption in deep UV than MgF2
20 layers may be insufficient with lower index contrast
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate under air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 repeated 10 times (20 finite layers total, starting with HfO2). Initialize thicknesses on a linear chirp from 140 nm (layer 1) to 50 nm (layer 20). Apply per-layer thickness bounds of ±10 nm around the chirp trajectory. Optimize all 20 thicknesses to maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing mean transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Evaluate coherent TMM response across 255-1100 nm spectrum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Material substitution from route_02's MgF2/HfO2 to HfO2/SiO2 pair based on evidence about HfO2/SiO2 UV filter performance and SiO2's superior UV transparency, testing whether material choice improvement outweighs potential index contrast reduction.
